taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Refresh-token family rotation, reuse response and atomicity
controls.source_trace: Track issuance, replacement and revocation as one transition. Determine whether reuse rejects only one request or invalidates the intended family and downstream sessions.
controls.implementation_branch: Record the issuer policy for token-family reuse, allowed concurrency and any grace window. Do not assume every access token must be revoked on refresh reuse. Inspect atomic replacement and the exact descendants still usable after a detected replay, using synthetic local state rather than live token guessing.
controls.operational_method: Trace family ID, predecessor, replacement token and commit/delivery state. If rotation commits but the response is lost, a retry can be legitimate under an explicit grace/idempotency contract; distinguish it from two independently successful descendants exceeding policy. Use deterministic local interleaving and transport-loss simulation, then record which family members remain usable without treating every reuse event as proven theft.
controls.controlled_verification: Replay one previously consumed synthetic refresh token and inspect family state; use deterministic local barriers for a race rather than live request bursts.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Two locally issued access tokens are not necessarily a defect if policy explicitly allows overlap; record actual reuse policy and validity.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Implement atomic family transitions and the declared reuse response, then verify normal refresh and reuse handling.
